newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia seeks to resolve problem of Minfin freezes.
newsitem.headline: Russia seeks to resolve problem of Minfin freezes.

text.p: The Finance Ministry, central bank and Federal Securities Comission on Wednesday called on Russia's courts to resolve all problems surrounding frozen MinFin bonds, warning that the row was damaging Russia's image abroad.
"There have been various cases of MinFin bonds freezes where the owners had nothing to do with criminal cases being investigated," the three bodies said in a joint statement.
"The consequence of it was a serious conflict on the MinFin market which has a negative impact on Russia's reputation as international debtor and issuing of Eurobonds."
Russian police froze $10.729 million nominal of MinFin bonds in May, the latest in a series of freezes which have unsettled the market.

Last year, the authorities froze about $74 million of bonds as part of an investigation into stolen bonds. Most of the paper was subsequently unfrozen, but only after the move shook confidence in the market, causing a fall in prices.
The total nominal value of all outstanding MinFin bonds is $11 billion.

The statement called on the judicial organs to correct mistakes made by police when they froze the MinFins if the securities had been bought in good faith. It said legislation should be changed to make the new policy workable.
